title: Panoptes measurement protocol v1
thesis: AI-text attribution is a measurement problem: the evidential meaning of a detector score depends on the generating population, prevalence, domain, manipulation history, provenance, and calibration cohort. Panoptes measures that evidential strength and its failure modes rather than ranking another detector.

research_questions.name: Calibration
research_questions.question: When Panoptes reports a probability of AI participation, does that probability correspond to empirical frequency under a declared population?

research_questions.name: Distribution shift
research_questions.question: How much does AI-text attribution degrade when the domain, generator, prompt, time period, or editing process changes?

research_questions.name: Evidence aggregation
research_questions.question: Does explicit calibration, Bayesian evidence aggregation, uncertainty estimation, and abstention improve trustworthiness over conventional classifier scores?

research_questions.name: Reproducibility
research_questions.question: Can the full experimental claim be independently verified from cryptographically committed datasets, model artifacts, manifests, and results?

tasks.human_only: No AI generation or substantive AI rewriting.
tasks.ai_generated: The majority or entirety of the content was generated by an AI system.
tasks.ai_assisted: A human authored the content but AI substantially generated or modified portions.
tasks.unknown: Available evidence is insufficient for a supported attribution.

outputs.ai_participation: P(AI generated or substantially modified the content). This is not interchangeable with P(AI-generated).
outputs.ai_generation: P(the majority or entirety of the content was generated by an AI system).
outputs.source_family: Conditional similarity among supported generator families plus an explicit unknown/open-set score.

split_rules.hard_rule: Train, calibration, and test are separate. Never fit or tune the calibration layer on the final test set.
split_rules.grouping: Splits are disjoint on prompt/group, and additionally on author and source/story when those fields exist.
split_rules.nested_grouped_cv: Default when n_groups < 30. Outer folds are untouched test groups; inner splits separate train from calibration.
split_rules.unseen_generator: Source-family attribution trains on known families and tests held-out families as unknown-source rejection.
split_rules.leakage: Official publisher splits are audited and never used when they leak groups.

evidence_pipeline: probability calibration on an independent calibration set
likelihood-ratio calibration using declared cohort prevalence

power.note: The existing two-proportion gate remains the admission rule for neural-tier comparisons. Calibration and transport claims require the same group-disjoint protocol even when the neural gate fails.

priors.rule: Detector evidence (LR) and posterior probability are not the same quantity. Every reported posterior names its prior.

provenance_levels.P3: Cryptographically signed generation receipt (e.g. verified C2PA).
provenance_levels.P4: Independently verifiable execution (hash-pinned run, Merkle commitment, optional OpenTimestamps).

stylometry_hypotheses: research/hypotheses.json remains the H1-H6 stylometry battery. Those tests are not the primary scientific claims of this protocol.
what_not_to_claim: Panoptes is a highly accurate AI detector.
ECE discounts or mathematically rescales a reported posterior.
Segment residuals that fail to reject autocorrelation prove segment independence.
Source-family similarity is exact model identity.
A negative watermark test is evidence of human authorship.
